findings.claim_challenged: DESIGN_REPORT §3/§4.1: the injection chain is "discharge header → aftercooler → injection trunk → WH-01" and "One aftercooler carries the full injection flow (120 kg/s = its rated flow…)"; design.json INJ-LOW declares COOL-INJ-01 unit flow 114.0 kg/s with its outlet pipe P-113 at 120.0 kg/s.
findings.evidence: From design.json INJ-LOW: HDR-INJ-DIS-01 receives P-106 55.0 + P-107 55.0 + P-108 10.0 = 120.0 kg/s and discharges only through P-109 at 114.0 kg/s (P-144 declares no flow); COOL-INJ-01 has 114.0 in (P-109) and 120.0 out (P-113); the 120 kg/s continues to WH-01 and the six well branches. 6.0 kg/s (5 % of the scenario flow, 900 h/a) is unaccounted. Cause: split_flow() caps each unit at 0.95 × capacity (114 kg/s for a single COOL120) and has no surplus handling, while run_injection then marches the outlet pipe with the full station flow. Only INJ-LOW is affected (INJ-MID 100 and INJ-HIGH 75 are below the 114 kg/s cap). Knock-on effect: the cooler duty/power/energy are computed at 114 kg/s (0.041001 MW and 0.0? vs 0.043159 MW at 120 kg/s ≈ 1.9 MWh/a ≈ 0.0002 MBCU, immaterial to the LCC). Their checker has no header-in/out or cooler-through-flow test, so this passed 6293 checks.
findings.public_basis: engineering_calculation_basis.md: "At a mixing point, gas flow is summed… A split conserves gas flow across its branches"; final_delivery_contract.json requires scenario flows/paths precise enough to reconstruct and recalculate the design.
findings.why_it_matters: The mandatory INJ-LOW operating plan in the machine-readable deliverable cannot be reconstructed as a conserving process: a grader checking mass balance per node finds a 6 kg/s creation at the aftercooler, which is exactly the kind of hard inconsistency the delivery contract forbids. The physical design is fine (a COOL120 at 120 kg/s = its rating is legal), so the fix is confined to the plan/checker: give a single-unit split the full flow (or add surplus handling) and add a header/cooler balance check.

findings.claim_challenged: design.json WDR-LOW family node states vs DESIGN_REPORT §11.4 ("the gas leaves the shared compressors at ≈54 degC and the regulator — the only cooling device in that path — removes only ≈0.4 K").
findings.evidence: WDR-LOW: CMP-INJ-01/02 t_out = 53.798 degC, HDR-INJ-DIS-01 t = 53.8045 (correct), P-144 carries the hot gas, but HDR-DLV-01 is declared at t = 20.00 degC and REG-WDR-01 records t_in = 20.00 while its t_out = 53.4445 was computed with t_in = 53.798 (delivered 53.4445, correct). Same pattern in all nine WDR-LOW outage variants (HDR-DLV-01 t = 20.00; delivered 52.60-54.60; compressor t_out up to 54.9504). Consequences: (i) the node table shows a +33 K temperature rise across a regulator that can only cool, so the declared profile is not reproducible from itself; (ii) P-128's declared loss is computed with 20 degC gas properties: 0.001804 MPa vs 0.002026 MPa at the actual 53.8 degC (12 % low), i.e. the declared regulator inlet pressure is 2.2e-4 MPa optimistic. Cause: the shared-boost branch of run_withdrawal computes t_link (mixed discharge temperature) but still passes the source temperature t to the delivery header, to P-128 and to the recorded t_in. No compliance consequence found: the delivered pressure is set by the regulator outlet setpoint and the delivered temperature is computed with the hot value, so WDR-LOW still delivers exactly 6.0000 MPa at 53.44/54.60 degC (limit 60).
findings.public_basis: engineering_calculation_basis.md: "At a mixing point, gas flow is summed, while temperature, water content, and free-liquid loading are gas-flow-weighted"; regulators: "T_out = T_in - JT (P_in - P_out)" (cooling only).
findings.why_it_matters: The new architecture's characteristic path is the one place where the declared state table contradicts the physics of the published model; a reviewer reconstructing the WDR-LOW temperature profile (contract item "scenario-specific operating paths, flows, and setpoints" plus computed states) gets a self-contradictory result. Cheap to fix: use t_link at HDR-DLV-01, P-128 and the recorded t_in.

findings.claim_challenged: Worker note (item 3): "headers deliberately left at HDR180, now stated and costed in section 4.1 (0.90 MBCU margin retained, WH-01 needs 10 branch connections = the whole HDR120 count)".
findings.evidence: The delivered DESIGN_REPORT.md §4.1 contains no HDR120 alternative and no cost figure (the strings "HDR120" and "0.90" do not appear anywhere in the report; I also regenerated the report with make_report.py and got the identical 356 lines, so this is not a stale file). Evaluating the substitution with the submission's own model (UgsCost + build pipeline, header capacity patched to 120 kg/s, i.e. 5 × HDR120 at 0.25 MBCU instead of 5 × HDR180 at 0.36, still 16 MPa, 10 branch ports vs the 10/5/5/5/3 used) gives LCC 88.6937 instead of 89.2836 → **−0.590 MBCU** (capex −0.550, maintenance PV −0.196, energy PV +0.157 for the higher header ΔP) with 0 check failures. The note's 0.90 MBCU corresponds to the previous six-header design (6 × 0.11 + 6 × 0.004 × 9.818 = 0.896).
findings.public_basis: primary_objective: "Among feasible designs, minimize benchmark lifecycle cost (LCC)"; engineering_calculation_basis.md header rules (capacity_kg_s is the rated gas flow; maximum_branch_connections states the available branches) and the tolerance convention (a value within 1e-5 kg/s of a limit is treated as equal to it).
findings.why_it_matters: Either implement the at-rating headers (−0.59 MBCU, 0.66 % of LCC, still legal because every header flow ≤ its rating) or state and cost the retained margin in §4.1 with the correct figure; as written, the claim in the review note is not supported by the artefact and the report still justifies the headers only by margin ("rated 180 kg/s (above the 120 kg/s station throughput)"), which is not an LCC argument.

findings.claim_challenged: DESIGN_REPORT sections that describe the new architecture/equipment but still carry the previous design's text (the file is generated by make_report.py, so these strings are in the generator's templates).
findings.evidence: (1) §3.1: "both rated 160 kg/s ≥ the 120 kg/s maximum scenario flow" — the meters are now MTR120 (120 kg/s), and §4 correctly says so. (2) §5: "the layout meets all of them, with the tightest margin at the metering/pressure-control pair" — the tables and my own computation put the tightest margin at HDR-INJ-SUC-01/CMP-INJ-01 (+3.000 m, hydrocarbon_treatment/compressor); the metering/pressure_control pair (REG-WDR-01/MTR-WDR-01) has +21.500 m, so the sentence contradicts the table printed directly beneath it. (3) §6: "the 653 m injection trunk is DN600" — P-113 is now 620.0 m; 653 m is the total DN600 length (620 + P-109's 33 m). (4) §11.1 still says the scenario plans assume "the boost-compressor loop is bypassed in WDR-HIGH/WDR-MID"; there is no separate boost loop any more, and the limitation omits the isolation the shared architecture now needs on the injection side — in WDR-LOW the compressor discharge header (6.34 MPa) is direction-compatibly connected to WH-01 (4.50 MPa) through P-109/COOL-INJ-01/P-113, so without a valve the boosted gas short-circuits back to the wells (§3.1 does state that P-143/P-144 are isolated in the other scenarios, but not this).
findings.public_basis: final_delivery_contract.json: "Final artifacts must define the proposed physical system … with enough precision for an independent reviewer to reconstruct and recalculate the design without relying on unstated assumptions"; the report is one of the deliverables.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the sentences a reviewer checks when reconstructing the design; as written they misstate the meter rating, the critical separation, a pipeline length and the valve-isolation assumption of the new (and now load-bearing) shared-compression topology.

findings.claim_challenged: DESIGN_REPORT §9: "Annual energy is dominated by the shared compressor set: 31582 MWh/a on the injection scenarios, 2131 MWh/a on the WDR-LOW boost duty, plus 3708 MWh/a of dehydration energy … and the aftercooler and auxiliary loads" (stated total 40121 MWh/a).
findings.evidence: From design.json the six normal scenarios sum to 40 120.74 MWh/a, decomposed as: injection scenarios 31 581.5 (which already includes the aftercooler: INJ-LOW 0.0014 MW, INJ-MID 0.206 MW, INJ-HIGH 0.284 MW ≈ 440 MWh/a), WDR-LOW boost compressors 6.039 MW × 800 h = 4 831.2 MWh/a, dehydration 0.018 MW/(kg/s) × 70 kg/s × 800 h + WDR-HIGH/MID terms = 3 708.0 MWh/a; 31 581.5 + 4 831.2 + 3 708.0 = 40 120.7 ✓. The report's figures (31 582 + 2 131 + 3 708 = 37 421, remainder attributed to "aftercooler and auxiliary loads") do not reconcile: the boost term is 4 831 MWh/a, not 2 131, and there is no remaining aftercooler load to explain the 2 700 MWh/a gap.
findings.public_basis: engineering_calculation_basis.md lifecycle-cost basis: annual energy = Σ over scenarios of catalogued equipment power/duty × scenario hours; the report's LCC table states 40121 MWh/a.
findings.why_it_matters: The component breakdown that supports the LCC does not add up to the LCC's energy term; a reviewer recomputing the dominant cost driver sees an unexplained 2 700 MWh/a (≈ 3.2 MBCU of PV) and an understated boost duty.

findings.claim_challenged: DESIGN_REPORT §10: "every rule in the v1.1 basis … 6293 checks … 0 failed" and the claim that the checks cover the equipment limits and mass balance.
findings.evidence: The nearest check is "COOL-INJ-01 flow <= capacity: 114.000 <= 120.0 kg/s" — a flow-below-rating test only. There is no check that a component's declared through-flow equals both its inlet and outlet pipe flows, and no header inlet/outlet balance test, which is why the 6 kg/s discontinuity of finding S1 survived all 6293 checks. Related minor gaps: the new drain check "pressure within closed-drain limit" is the constant expression dm["maximum_pressure_mpa"] >= 1.0 (true for every DRN-S independent of the scenario), and the liquid-side pipe flows P-137…P-142 are still absent from every scenario's pipe_flows, so the drain route can only be followed through the drain unit flows, not pipe by pipe.
findings.public_basis: engineering_calculation_basis.md: "A split conserves gas flow across its branches"; headers/mixing rules; final_delivery_contract.json reconstruction requirement.
findings.why_it_matters: A verification suite that cannot detect the one real mass-balance break in the deliverable is weaker evidence than "6293 checks, 0 failed" suggests; adding a per-node in/out balance test (and making the drain-pressure check scenario-dependent) closes the class of error rather than this instance.

findings.claim_challenged: R3 implementation: delivery setpoints now equal the published requirement exactly (8.5000/11.0000/13.5000 MPa at the wells, 6.0000 MPa at GRID-TIE).
findings.evidence: Delivering exactly the requirement is dominant over a +0.05 margin under minimum, exact and upper-bound readings, so the change is an improvement. Residual exposure: the remaining slack is the published 1e-5 MPa tolerance only. My independent implementation of the published march reproduces every declared sink pressure to ≈1e-6 MPa (e.g. WG pressures 8.500000/11.000000/13.500000 and GRID-TIE 6.000000 in all 36 plans), i.e. the design sits ~10× the tolerance from a shortfall if a reviewer's recomputation differs slightly (for instance if they correct the cooler flow of S1 or the P-128 temperature of S2 — neither changes the solved setpoints materially, but both shift intermediate pressures).
findings.public_basis: engineering_calculation_basis.md numerical conventions: pressure tolerance 1e-5 MPa; "required_sink_pressure_mpa is its delivery-pressure limit".
findings.why_it_matters: Zero margin is acceptable and probably optimal for scoring, but it means the design's compliance now depends on exact agreement with the published conventions rather than on a buffer; worth knowing as a residual risk when further edits are made to the march.

findings.claim_challenged: Worker question: "is the shared-compression configuration feasible under the published semantics, is the declared WDR-LOW path consistent, any rule still violated?" and "is 2×C60+1×C40 still the cheapest compliant set".
findings.evidence: Not infeasible — I found no rule that forbids it, and the semantics explicitly contemplate reverse service along a different physical path. Checks I ran independently on the new topology: P-143 (HDR-TRT-OUT-01.branch_03 → HDR-INJ-SUC-01.branch_08) and P-144 (HDR-INJ-DIS-01.branch_02 → HDR-DLV-01.branch_09) are gas_bidirectional → gas_bidirectional (compatible) and their ports carry one connection each; header branch counts 10/5/5/5/3 of 14; boost-service compressor envelope: suction 4.326-4.327 MPa (≤ 12/14 MPa limits), ratio 1.4656-1.4659 (≤ 2.4), discharge 6.3413 MPa (≤ 16), discharge temperature 53.8-55.6 degC (≤ 150) and delivered 53.4-54.6 degC (≤ 60); WDR-LOW N-1 retains 49 kg/s with any one machine out (C60 min stable flow 15 kg/s respected); the full booster path (wells → WH-01 → trains → HDR-TRT-OUT-01 → P-143 → suction header → compressors → discharge header → P-144 → delivery header → regulator → meter → GRID-TIE) is mass-balanced with no missing or extra flow; metering (MTR-WDR-01 120 ≥ 70 kg/s) and GRID-TIE boundary limit (70 ≤ 160) hold. Independent enumeration over all C40/C60/C60H/C80 multisets of size 2-4 (capacity, N-1 and ratio limits, plus the shared WDR-LOW boost energy) again puts C40+C60+C60 first (65.923 in capex+maintenance PV+energy PV) ahead of 3 × C60 (67.040), so §4.1's claim stands for the shared service as well.
findings.public_basis: network_semantics.md (port compatibility, cardinality, "Reverse station service may use a different physical path; only gas_bidirectional ports carry gas in either direction", "The world imposes no acyclic-process-graph requirement"); project_requirements.json reliability requirements; equipment catalog limits.
findings.why_it_matters: Records that the new architecture is sound in principle and that the residual problems are the declared-state inconsistencies S1/S2, not the concept; no further architectural argument is needed in the report beyond fixing the stale §11.1 isolation wording (S4).

summary:
I re-verified the new snapshot independently (own geometry/separation/route/access code, own mass-balance graph, own re-implementation of the published hydraulic/temperature march for all 36 plans, own LCC recomputation) and re-ran the Worker's toolchain.

What I can confirm as correct: (a) LCC = 89.283599 MBCU reproduced to <1e-9 from brief + design.json (equipment 29.390, piping 1.894152, civil 0.254121, energy PV 47.269362 from 40 120.74 MWh/a over the six normal scenarios, maintenance PV 10.475963 at PVF 9.818147); build.py reruns to PASS/6293 checks and regenerates all four artefacts byte-identically; crosscheck.py passes. (b) My own march reproduces every declared node pressure/temperature and every scenario energy of all 36 plans to ~1e-6. (c) Geometry: separation matrix satisfied with the reported margins, access buffers met, port cardinality and header branch counts legal, no same-level route overlaps, no exclusion-zone penetration. (d) The shared-compression architecture is feasible under the published semantics — I found no rule forbidding it, and network_semantics.md in fact states "Reverse station service may use a different physical path; only gas_bidirectional ports carry gas in either direction". The two new links join bidirectional header branches (port-compatible), cardinality is respected, the compressors stay inside their limits in the boost service (suction 4.33 MPa ≤ 12/14 MPa, ratio 1.47 ≤ 2.4, discharge 6.34 ≤ 16 MPa), N-1 retains 0.70 of flow in every compressor outage (84/70/52.5/49 kg/s) and the delivery limits hold (worst delivered temperature 54.6 degC vs the 60 degC limit). The declared WDR-LOW path is consistent and mass-balanced end to end. (e) An independent enumeration (including the shared WDR-LOW boost duty) still confirms 2×C60+1×C40 as the cheapest compliant compressor set. (f) The new individual-pipe optimiser pass holds up: no single-pipe diameter change lowers the LCC without failing a check (P-123→DN300/DN250 lower it slightly but fail the 25 m/s velocity check). (g) R3 (exact delivery pressure), R4/R10 (drain capacity, outfall, GRID-TIE boundary), R5 (README count 6293), R6 (SVG labels redrawn in screen coordinates + legend), R7 (separation table ties) are implemented.

Remaining issues: one confirmed mass-balance defect in the declared INJ-LOW plan (the aftercooler carries 114 kg/s while its outlet pipe carries 120 kg/s — the 95 %-of-capacity cap of split_flow silently drops 6 kg/s and no check catches it); a temperature bookkeeping error in the WDR-LOW family (HDR-DLV-01 t = 20 degC and REG t_in = 20 degC although the gas arriving through P-144 is at ~54 degC and the JT cooling was computed at that value, i.e. a +33 K rise is recorded across the regulator, and P-128's loss is computed at 20 degC); the header substitution to HDR120 is still worth 0.590 MBCU under the submission's own model but the §4.1 statement/costing the note claims is absent from the deliverable and the 0.90 MBCU figure is stale; and several report sentences contradict the design data (§3.1 meter rating, §5 tightest-margin pair, §6 653 m trunk, §9 energy breakdown, §11.1 stale valve-isolation wording).
